Vivek / Marissa — quick guidance below (high level; happy to draft language for procurement):

- CSV: good. Add two columns we usually include for commercial signoffs: "Legal Basis" (e.g., Performance of Contract / Legitimate Interest) and "Data Categories" (e.g., telemetry, aggregated logs, KV cache). That avoids follow-ups from procurement.

- UK Addendum: Because Meditech is UK-based and will have UK-resident data, we should ask them to sign the UK Addendum in addition to the EU SCCs. That is the clearest route and reduces ambiguity with the ICO.

- TIA/DTIA exposure: Operationally we do two things:
   1) We keep a TIA record for any *persistent* cross-border destination (US backups, analytics providers).
   2) For transient compute hops (EU compute for UK-resident data where the data does not persist in the US beyond ephemeral caches), we document technical safeguards and schedule a quarterly sampling TIA note instead of a full DTIA.

So for Meditech: require UK Addendum + EU SCCs; attach the subprocessor CSV (with the 2 additional columns); and include a one-page TIA summary that states we will: (a) keep DTIA for US backup destinations, and (b) treat ephemeral compute as covered by technical mitigations with quarterly sampling.

I can draft the one-page TIA summary and the extra CSV columns — will send a draft in ~90 minutes.

-Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
